Timeline::microsecond¶

Back to Timeline API Reference

Signature¶

Series Timeline::microsecond() const

microsecond() is the sole public spelling.

Read The Fraction At Microsecond Resolution¶

microsecond() returns the fractional second measured in whole microseconds. Its valid range is 0 through 999'999, its dtype is int32, and its shape matches the Timeline. Absent instants produce -1.

The conversion is truncation, not rounding:

microsecond = nanosecond / 1,000

Consequently, nanoseconds below one microsecond are deliberately discarded.

Example: Observe The Truncation¶

const auto events = pluss::timeline::make({
    "2020-12-31T23:59:59.123456789Z",
    "2021-01-01T00:00:00.987654321Z",
    "2024-02-29T06:07:08.009010011Z",
    "",
});

pluss::series::print(std::cout, events.microsecond());

Output¶

Series(shape=[4], strides=[1], dtype=int32, platform=cpu, numel=4, contiguous=true)
data=[123456, 987654, 9010, -1]

The first fraction loses its trailing 789 nanoseconds; the third loses 11. That is expected precision reduction, not floating-point error.

When To Use It¶

Use this extractor when an interface, grouping key, or storage format is defined in whole microseconds. If you only want timestamps displayed with six digits, prefer formatting: extraction converts the fraction to ordinary numeric data and discards the temporal type.

Gotchas And Failure Modes¶

  • No rounding occurs at the half-microsecond boundary.

  • The value is within the current second, not since the epoch.

  • Once lower nanosecond digits are discarded, this result cannot reconstruct the original timestamp exactly.
